title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover to prevent thrashing under spike
author: Ethan Cole
description: Motivation: Production incidents on 2026-02-14 and 2026-02-15 showed SLO-enforcer thrashing during sudden multi-region traffic spikes. The enforcer would rapidly toggle load-shedding and trigger regional circuit-breaker failovers in a feedback loop, causing large request drops and recovery instability. This hotfix adds a controlled exponential backoff window to SLO enforcer state transitions, stabilizes regional failover coordination, and tightens health-check coupling to avoid premature failovers. Changes: 1) SLO enforcer: introduce per-entity transition cooldown with jittered exponential backoff, configurable via runtime flags with safe defaults; 2) Circuit breaker coordinator: add consensus step to ensure only one region initiates failover per affected customer within a sliding window; 3) Load-shedding policy: prefer graceful shedding (priority-based token limits) over abrupt hard rejects when KB cache hits are high; 4) Health checks: require two consecutive degraded polls before opening a region-level CB; 5) Tests: add unit tests for backoff math and integration canary test that simulates region outage and traffic spike to validate no thrash. Rollout plan: deploy to canary region (us-west-2) behind feature flag for 24 hours, monitor SLOs and circuit-breaker metrics, then staged rollout to other regions with 10% increments. Backwards compatibility: default flags match current behavior but enable safer behavior by default in new installs; operators can tune via console or config. Checklist: [x] Design review (ENG-1253) completed [x] Unit tests added [x] Integration canary test added [x] E2E smoke in canary passed [x] Docs updated in runbook. Notes: This PR is a hotfix and was fast-tracked; it intentionally limits surface area and keeps defaults conservative while allowing operators to opt-in to more aggressive throttling strategies later.
commits: Fix: add transition cooldown and exponential backoff for SLO enforcer
Fix: tighten health-check gating to require two consecutive failures
Test: add canary integration test simulating regional outage
Docs: update runbook and runtime flags

infra/feature-flags.yaml - add slo_enforcer_backoff and cb_coordination flags
review_comments: Priya Desai: We should ensure the default backoff window is small enough for interactive customers but large enough to avoid thrash. Please add metrics to verify cooldowns are effective.
Ethan Cole: Added cooldown metrics (slo_enforcer.cooldown_seconds and slo_enforcer.cooldown_events) and dashboard links in the description. Default is 15s with 2x exponential growth capped at 5m.
Marisa Chen: Integration test looks good; please make sure coordinator consensus uses existing gossip channel and not a new RPC path to avoid rollout complexity.
Ethan Cole: Switched to existing gossip channel and added unit tests for message ordering; also included a feature flag so we can rollback instantly if necessary.
Anders Holm: LGTm pending CI flake fix; please address lint failure in coordinator file.
Ethan Cole: Fixed lint and rebased onto main; CI rerun passed.

hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover to prevent thrashing under spike

- add per-entity cooldown/backoff
- coordinator consensus step for region failover
- graceful load-shedding path
- health-check gating hardened
- integration and unit tests

Closes ENG-1253, SRE-67

Stage rollout across regions with 10% increments after canary verification

release_notes: Hotfix: Prevents SLO-enforcer thrashing during sudden spikes by adding cooldown/backoff and stabilizing regional failover coordination. Includes default-safe flags and new metrics to observe cooldown behavior.
notes_for_ops: Feature flags: slo_enforcer_backoff.enabled=true, cb_coordination.enabled=true. Default cooldown initial: 15s, multiplier: 2x, cap: 300s. To rollback: disable flags and redeploy enforcer binary from v2026.02.10 build.
